content:
Neither Anthracnose (pod/stem lesions on mature plants) nor SDS (interveinal chlorosis/necrosis on leaves) match the test image.

The test image shows a young soybean seedling with:
- Stem damage/constriction at the soil line
- Dead, dried lower leaves/cotyledons
- The lesion appears dry and sunken, not water-soaked
- Upper portion still has some green growth
- Plant appears to be collapsing at the base

This matches **Rhizoctonia** — characterized by reddish-brown, sunken, firm and dry lesions on hypocotyls at the soil line. The dry canker can girdle the seedling and cause collapse. This is distinguished from Pythium (water-soaked, soft rot) and Phytophthora (chocolate-brown discoloration extending up the stem).
